    Docs / Security reviewSource: docs/security-review.md

    Multi-machine secrets: independent review brief

    Status: independent review pending. The version 2 protocol remains experimental. Repository tests, sanitizer runs and this brief are preparation for review; they are not an independent assessment or cryptographic sign-off.

    Scope and trust boundaries#

    Review a named source commit and the exact source hashes from tests/release/security_evidence.rb. Cover both successful operations and failure recovery across the encrypted store, machine-local key backend, plaintext session cache, generated shell loader, backups and synchronization. The wire/storage contract is in config-reference.md.

    Boundary Intended property Relevant source
    Constants → ciphertext Value authentication, name binding, nonce generation and run-only handling src/secrets_store.odin
    Backend → process Private master key and identity storage; per-data-dir separation src/keystore.odin
    Synced header → cached key Explicit first adoption; authenticated recipient and rotation state src/secrets_recipients.odin
    Recipient encoding → wrapped key Correct X25519, HKDF and AEAD composition; canonical encodings src/age.odin
    Encrypted store → shell Private cache directories/files, invalidation, quoting and limited exposure src/secrets_store.odin, src/init_generator.odin, src/shell.odin
    Write/restore → durable state Locking, backups, atomic replacement and interrupted-operation recovery src/atomic_io.odin, src/backup.odin

    Version 2 uses age-formatted X25519 identities and age's recipient derivation, but wraps a 32-byte wayu data key inside wayu's JSON container. It is not a standard age file. Compare with the age specification. Recovery uses Argon2id with the fixed parameters documented in the config reference; compare the choice and implementation with RFC 9106.

    Questions for the assessor#

    • Does deterministic recipient-stanza derivation provide the intended authentication without unsafe key/nonce reuse or cross-protocol interactions?
    • Do adoption, rotation proofs and machine-local recipient/removal history enforce the stated trust model through offline periods and concurrent writes?
    • Are recovery identity encryption, parameter validation, secret wiping and error handling appropriate for the supported platforms and Odin runtime?
    • Are v1 → v2 migration, rekey, backup restore and crashes recoverable without accepting an unverified key or losing the last decryptable copy?
    • Does every generated shell maintain the same private-cache and run-only semantics, including logout, shared runtime dirs and sync replacement?

    Known limits to assess, not stronger claims#

    • A compromised logged-in user or process with its keys can read secrets. The file backend does not protect against reading the whole home directory.
    • Session caches are plaintext, owner-only files until invalidated or locked. A sync replacement preserving an older mtime can leave the old cache in use.
    • Replays of individual values under the same data key are not detected. Trust before first adoption cannot come from the synced file alone.
    • Removed machines may retain old plaintext and keys. A machine that has not observed removal can accept a competing signed rotation from an old holder. Upstream credentials and a known recovery passphrase need separate rotation.

    These limits are already described in the configuration reference. Review whether their visibility and operational recovery are adequate.

    Evidence and completion criteria#

    Run ruby tests/release/security_evidence.rb from a built checkout. It records source hashes and runs existing unit and secrets integration tests in temporary homes. It uses fixture secrets and file/test backends, not production keys. The unit suite includes external X25519 vectors, parser, pinning, recovery and rotation checks. CI separately runs AddressSanitizer integration tests on Linux. CI retains a source-only manifest alongside the unit, integration and TUI outputs in test-evidence-<runner> artifacts. The manifest labels itself as source metadata; the surrounding job's success determines the test result.

    Before removing experimental status, retain a review report with assessor and date, commit/hashes, reviewed platforms and backends, exclusions, findings and severity, remediation commits, and assessor verification of remediation. Track unresolved findings explicitly. A maintainer must approve promotion after that evidence exists. Report privately through SECURITY.md.
